title: The Eternal Chess Game
next_chapter_hook: When Cang Yutian's first piece fell onto the chessboard, a mountain range in the mortal realm collapsed with a thunderous roar. Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply—that was the direction where Su Qingyao was cultivating.

text.content: The Tianji Record Fragment on his chest quivered violently, as if some ancient beast slumbering for ten thousand years was being awakened. Chen Ji felt a scalding power surge from the fragment, racing along his meridians straight into his mind. Countless fragmented images flickered before his eyes—starfields from ten millennia past, a burning altar, two silhouettes with their backs turned to all living beings seated opposite each other at a chessboard. He tried to grasp these images, but they slipped through his fingers like sand.

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian walked slowly toward the floating celestial map chessboard, his aged voice reverberating through the void: 'Ten thousand years ago, in that game, your father Chen Xuan and I were the Chess Players. We wagered on the dominion of the Heavenly Dao, and what we lost was... everything.' He turned to look at Chen Ji, a complex emotion flickering in his eyes. 'Now the chess game has reopened, but the Chess Player has become you. This is the choice of the Tianji Record, and also the cycle of fate.'

text.content: A wave of dizziness washed over Chen Ji. He watched as the celestial map chessboard behind Cang Yutian gradually became clear—it was no ordinary chessboard, but a grand star map with the entire mortal realm as its pieces. Every star corresponded to a person's destiny, and among them, several exceptionally bright stars were flickering with familiar radiance.

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian raised his hand and traced an illusory line above the chessboard, and the stars began to move: 'The rules are simple. Your destiny is the piece, the entire mortal realm is the board. Each move will alter the causalities in reality. When I place a piece, a region in the mortal realm crumbles; when you place a piece, you may rewrite one person's fate.' His voice turned ice-cold. 'And the stakes? Everyone you care about, plus the survival of all thirty-three realms in this mortal world.'

text.content: Chen Ji's heart sank heavily. He saw blurry silhouettes emerge on the chessboard—Su Qingyao's cold figure standing alone at the mountain gate of Tianqing Sect, Ye Qing bound by chains on the altar of the Demonic Holy Sect, even his long-lost sister Chen Nian, sealed within a cocoon of light, unable to move. What was far more terrifying than what he could see—the mountains and rivers of the entire mortal realm were all presented on the chessboard, every inch of land potentially utterly erased by this single game.

dialogue.content: 'Do you see it?' Cang Yutian's voice carried a hint of mockery, 'Your Tianji Record lets you foresee three hours ahead, yet you cannot see any possibility beyond this chess game. Because this game... is itself the origin of the Tianji Record.' He pointed to the chaotic mass at the center of the chessboard, 'What Chen Xuan lost ten thousand years ago was himself. And now, you must use the same wager to play against me again.'

text.content: Chen Ji's fists slowly tightened. He could feel the fragment against his chest was so hot it was almost burning through his skin. Mo Xiansheng's broken voice rang in his mind: 'Boy, this game... you must win. Not for me, not for any Heavenly Dao—for the people you care about.' He took a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down, and began rapidly analyzing the situation before him.

However, what truly made him despair were those brightest stars on the chessboard. Chen Ji recognized them—that was Su Qingyao, that was Ye Qing, that was Ling Yuan, that was Han Lie, even Chen Nian he had never met but had been searching for all along. Each person occupied a crucial position on the chessboard, each person's fate tightly bound by this game. All his arrangements, all his hidden lines, had in this moment become leverage for Cang Yutian to threaten him.

choice.prompt: Faced with this unimaginable chess gambling game, Chen Ji must respond before Cang Yutian. His choice will determine the tone of this Eternal Chess Game—whether to take a risky acceptance, or to cautiously probe?

choices.text: Go all-in and accept the chess game
choices.description: Since there is no way out, might as well wager everything and confront Cang Yutian directly, trading life for life, chess for heaven.
choices.visible_cost: The fates of all people one cares about become the wager
choices.visible_reward: Gain the qualification to play against the will of the Heavenly Dao
choices.risk_hint: Once defeated, never to rise again

text.content: Chen Ji stepped forward abruptly, a resolute gleam flashing in his eyes: 'Since the chess game from ten thousand years ago was never concluded, then I shall play another game with you!' His voice echoed through the void, and the fragment on his chest burst forth with unprecedented radiance, resonating distantly with the star map on the chessboard. The entire space trembled at this moment, as if thundering for the opening of this Eternal Chess Game.

dialogue.content: A flicker of appreciation crossed Cang Yutian's eyes: 'Good! Truly a son of Chen Xuan, possessing such boldness.' He raised his hand, and those blurry fate projections on the chessboard instantly became crystal clear, every detail rendered with perfect clarity. 'Then let us begin. You hold black, I hold white. This first move... you play first.'

choices.description: Do not rashly accept, first use words to probe Cang Yutian's bottom line, seeking possible flaws or negotiating space.
choices.visible_cost: May provoke the will of the Heavenly Dao
choices.visible_reward: Obtain more hidden information about the chess game's rules

text.content: Chen Ji did not respond immediately, but slowly closed his eyes. His consciousness sank into the fragment on his chest, rapidly communicating with Mo Xiansheng's remaining will. After a moment, he opened his eyes, his gaze becoming profound: 'Ten thousand years ago, you lost that game. So I would like to know—is the chessboard itself also within the stakes?'

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian's expression changed slightly, then burst into laughter: 'Good lad, being able to remain calm in such a situation. Truly one chosen by the Tianji Record.' His laughter gradually subsided, a dangerous glint flickering in his eyes. 'Since you wish to know, I shall tell you—this chessboard was jointly constructed by me and the Tianji Record, and it is not included in the stakes. But every move you make... I can see it all.'

text.content: Chen Ji stared intently at the familiar lights and shadows on the chessboard, his mind racing through calculations. He noticed that beside each fate projection there was a string of faint numbers—the lifespan markers displayed by the Tianji Record. Su Qingyao's markers were slowly draining away, Ye Qing's were fluctuating violently, but Chen Nian's... were completely blurred, as if deliberately obscured by some force.

dialogue.content: "I have one question." Chen Ji's voice was terrifyingly calm. "Ten thousand years ago, my father lost himself. Then why are his... fragments of soul sealed within this fragment?" He watched Cang Yutian's reaction closely. "What exactly did you do to him?"

text.content: Cang Yutian's expression turned intrigued. "Do you truly wish to know?" He swept his hand across the chessboard, summoning Chen Xuan's indistinct figure, bound by countless chains in the board's central chaos. "He wasn't destroyed—he simply became part of the game. Just as you are about to become." Chen Ji felt dizzy, noticing the chains' pattern perfectly matched the fragment's design on his chest.

Just then, a faint light flickered at the chessboard's edge. Chen Ji saw Su Qingyao's fate projection trembling violently, as if sensing something. Her lips parted slightly, and though no sound emerged, Chen Ji understood her silent warning—"Don't agree." Ye Qing's projection also shifted, her eyes reflecting a familiar determination, signaling a readiness to sacrifice everything.

choice.prompt: Seeing their struggle, Chen Ji's heart was deeply moved. He had to make a choice before Cang Yutian—whether to heed their warning and refuse this gamble, or to win this chess game at all costs to protect them.

choices.description: Even if this was a death sentence, even if it meant repeating his father's fate, he would fight a path of survival for them.
choices.visible_reward: Winning the chess game can rewrite everyone's fate

text.content: Chen Ji drew a deep breath, slowly extracting the fragment from his chest. It ignited in his palm, transforming into a pitch-black chess piece. He could sense Su Qingyao and Ye Qing's gazes piercing through the void, watching him—those eyes held worry, trust, and anticipation. He smiled faintly and pressed the piece onto the board: "This move, I make for them."

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian gazed at the piece in Chen Ji's palm, a flash of surprise crossing his eyes. "You've condensed a physical chess piece using your Heavenly Fate?" He shook his head with a knowing laugh. "Interesting. Your father began in exactly the same way." He raised his hand, and a white piece appeared in his palm. "Then I shall respond to your move."

choices.description: Not accepting the existing gamble rules, attempting to break this deadly deadlock by exploiting the chessboard's own rules.
choices.visible_reward: Potentially discovering hidden rules of the chess game
choices.risk_hint: Potentially angering Cang Yutian and worsening the situation

text.content: Chen Ji didn't rush to make his move. Instead, he delved into the fragment again with his consciousness. This time, he saw further—he witnessed the very moment the chessboard formed, saw the final scene of his father's confrontation with Cang Yutian, and more importantly, spotted a deliberately overlooked detail: the chessboard required a "witness," and the witness... need not be a player.

dialogue.content: Mr. Mo's voice echoed in his mind, carrying a hint of satisfaction: "Boy, you've finally understood. The chessboard needs a witness, and I... am the remnant soul of a witness left from long ago. If you're willing, I can bear part of the chess game's backlash for you. But the price is—you must find the key to breaking the deadlock within three moves."

text.content: Just as Chen Ji contemplated the deeper meaning of Mr. Mo's words, the entire chessboard suddenly shook violently. Cang Yutian's expression changed for the first time. He looked up at the void, his ancient voice tinged with disbelief: "How could she appear at this moment..." Chen Ji followed his gaze and saw at the board's very edge, a nearly completely dimmed star was slowly brightening—and its position corresponded precisely to where Chen Nian was.

Chen Ji's heart clenched tightly. That star should have been completely blurred. What force had caused it to reappear? He looked closer and noticed a faint halo surrounding the star—it was the aura of the Tianji Record! His sister Chen Nian had actually resonated with the Tianji Record fragment? At this moment, he finally understood why finding Chen Nian had been so difficult—because she herself was part of the Tianji Record, the "Heavenly Fate Lock Key" taken by the Holy Sect to repair the fragment.

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian's voice broke Chen Ji's reverie: "It seems you've discovered her significance." His finger pointed at Chen Nian's fate projection. "She is the lost page of the Tianji Record, one of the keys to solving this chess game. But also... the greatest variable." He looked at Chen Ji, a meaningful light flickering in his eyes. "Do you want to save her?"

text.content: Chen Ji didn't answer. He simply stared intently at Chen Nian's rekindled star on the chessboard, his heart churning with complex emotions. He remembered the night years ago when his sister was kidnapped, her cries of distress. He remembered every clue he had secretly traced over these years. And he remembered the vow he made to ensure her safety at all costs. Now, she was right here on this board, in this life-or-death gamble. He had to win—for her, and for everyone he cared about.

choice.prompt: Cang Yutian's question struck directly at the deepest obsession in Chen Ji's heart. He had to make a choice—whether to use his sister's safety as the core wager, or remaincalm and prevent emotions from clouding his judgment.

choices.text: Using Chen Nian as the chess eye
choices.description: Putting all the chips on his sister, arranging the chess game around her fate projection, even if the cost is sacrificing everything else.
choices.visible_reward: If successful, it can directly break the balance of the chess game
choices.risk_hint: Too obvious intentions may be targeted by Cang Yutian

text.content: Chen Ji slowly pushed the black chess piece in his hand toward Chen Nian's fate projection: "The gambled game ten thousand years ago, my father may have lost because he was too benevolent." His voice was ice-cold and firm, "This round, I will not make the same mistake. Since she is the key, I will put all my bets on her."

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian watched Chen Ji's movements, a meaningful smile appearing at the corner of his mouth: "Interesting. Your father chose to sacrifice himself to protect everyone back then, and you... chose to go all in." He raised his hand, and the white chess piece fell, "But do you know, this is exactly what I wanted?"

choices.description: Not exposing the obsession with his sister before Cang Yutian, using other chess pieces as cover, secretly arranging and waiting for the right moment.
choices.visible_cost: Temporarily giving up the best opportunity to save Chen Nian
choices.visible_reward: Maintaining strategic initiative, not letting Cang Yutian see through the intentions
choices.risk_hint: May miss the opportunity to break the situation

text.content: Chen Ji's fingers paused slightly, then he drew the black chess piece back into his palm. He looked at Cang Yutian, a hint of mockery flickering in his eyes: "Are you probing me?" He casually placed the chess piece in an inconspicuous spot on the edge of the board, "Chen Nian's affairs, I have my own arrangements. No need for the Heavenly Dao to concern itself."

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian raised an eyebrow, seemingly somewhat surprised by Chen Ji's composure: "Oh? It seems you're not as easily provoked as you appear." He lowered his head to look at the board, "However, this position you've chosen... is to buy time?" His voice carried a hint of amusement, "An interesting tactic."

text.content: The moment Chen Ji's black chess piece fell on the board, the entire mortal realm sensed the opening of this ancient gamble spanning ten thousand years. At the summit of Tianqing Sect, Su Qingyao suddenly opened her eyes, feeling the Inner Sect token at her chest burning intensely - that protective charm Chen Ji had left her was sensing its master's fate fluctuation. And in the forbidden grounds of the Demonic Path Holy Sect, one of the chains binding Ye Qing suddenly broke. She raised her head, gazing toward some invisible distance, a relieved smile appearing at the corner of her lips. The chess game has begun, there is no turning back.
